messages:
Maria: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a 'roofline' style microbench for onboarding to classify models as memory-bound vs compute-bound. The goal is to pick default kernels/quant profiles and detect models that will thrash KV cache. Thoughts?

Kevin: SGTM. How heavy is the bench? we need to keep onboarding cheap for public hosted users. Do you have a staging runner in mind? :thinking:

ingest-bot: Model 'falcon-x-128k-v2' registered by @Maria (id: m-98372). Artifact: s3://redwood-models/m-98372/

Maria: The bench is intentionally tiny — 20 iterations per shape, shapes: seq=16/64/512 plus a cold->hot KV cache sweep. We measure tokens/sec, peak GPU memory, and p50/p95 latency. Cost estimate: ~0.5 GPU-min per run on an A10G-equivalent. We can gate it to only run for models >100M params or on request.

Jia: Also we need stronger checksum / shard-validator for sharded checkpoints. We keep seeing ragged shards and XLA packing differences. Suggest adding a quick shim: `rcheck validate --model-dir $DIR` that checks shard byte sizes + checksummed names and outputs a minimal manifest.

Sam: Agree on both. Reminder: last month a new 70B variant caused severe KV cache thrash in Dedicated canaries because it had big attention heads + long default seq. We should include a synthetic long-context decode test to exercise KV cache eviction. That would catch LRU thrash patterns.

Kevin: For reproducibility we should fix seeds and env in the bench. e.g. `python -m ri_bench --model-dir /tmp/m --seq 512 --iters 20 --seed 42 --device gpu`. We should record the exact container image + CUDA/cuDNN versions.

Maria: Good call — bench output will include a small metadata blob: image, cuda, cudnn, kernels used, hw fingerprint. We'll store the bench artifact alongside the model manifest and expose a short URL in model metadata.

Jia: Note: hardware fingerprinting matters. The same model on older Ampere vs H100 can flip from memory-bound to compute-bound. We should tag bench results with perf labels per hw class and add a "router_label" key customers can use to prefer a variant.

Sam: What are pass/fail thresholds? p95 latency < X for seq16/64, tokens/sec > Y for seq512? We need to avoid hardcoded numbers that block good models. Maybe three buckets: green/yellow/red with human review for red.

Maria: Proposal: green = meets both latency and throughput baselines for the target tier; yellow = within 20% of baseline or has high memory but stable perf; red = fails stability or shows KV thrash. Red requires manual signoff by infra + ML. I'll draft thresholds and share.

Kevin: We should also add a nondeterminism check for sampling: `same-seed` deterministic microtest for 5 runs. If output tokens diverge too much on greedy inference we've got issues.

Jia: One more: shard layout validation should include an expected tensor list (name, shape, dtype) vs stored metadata. Many failing models had mismatched dtype orders (fp16 vs bf16). Validator can emit a normalized manifest to drive conversion jobs.

Sam: Operationally, tie this into canary rollout: bench->validator pass required to auto-canary. If bench is yellow, allow canary with reduced traffic and automatic fallback to a smaller policy.

Maria: OK I'll fill out a short RFC with: bench harness spec, shard-validator CLI, pass/yellow/red thresholds, metadata schema, and canary gating flow. Volunteers to review? @Kevin @Jia @Sam?

Kevin: I'll review and add cost knobs (skip bench for low-risk models).

Jia: Happy to review validator spec and provide examples of malformed shards we saw.

Sam: I'll wire the canary gating and fallback policy into rollout infra once we have the hook.

Maria: Thanks — I'll open the RFC and drop a link here when ready. :thumbsup:
